paper_title: Exploring Text Specific and Blackbox Fairness
core_problem: Ensuring fairness and preventing discrimination in multimodal clinical machine learning tasks, specifically addressing equalized odds on text and tabular data.
methodology_summary: Investigating a modality-agnostic fairness algorithm (equalized odds post-processing) and a text-specific fairness algorithm (debiased clinical word embeddings). The core approach involves ensembling classifiers trained on structured and unstructured data.
empirical_results: The dual modality ensemble improves performance and mitigates unfairness relative to constituent components. Equalized odds post-processing diminishes group-specific disparities in TP and TN rates, but this comes with a degradation in AUC. Word embedding debiasing also helps reduce TP/TN discrepancies.
explicit_limitations: The ensemble's performance improvements do not directly translate to fairness improvements; improving fairness (via EO post-processing) usually results in a degradation of performance (AUC).
